headline: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia sign 'Badr' defence cooperation pact
standfirst: Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said.
body_markdown:
Pakistan, Qatar, Turkiye and Indonesia on Wednesday signed a multilateral pact to promote cooperation in defence production and capabilities, the Turkish defence ministry said. The signing took place in Qatar, with ministers of the four countries attending the ceremony. Defence Minister Khawaja Asif represented Pakistan at the signing. (Dawn Pakistan)

**Times of India Top Stories** adds: Türkiye, Qatar, Indonesia and Pakistan have signed the Badr memorandum to strengthen defence cooperation and develop strategic partnerships, the Turkish National Defence Ministry said on Wednesday. The agreement was signed in Doha by the defence ministers of the four countries, including Turkish National Defence Minister Yasar Guler, Qatar’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of State for Defence Affairs Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman bin Hasan Al Thani, Indonesian Deputy Defence Minister Yusuf Jauhari and Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif.

**Anadolu Agency** adds: Badr memorandum aims to boost military production, strengthen defense capabilities, and expand cooperation in training, research, and development

**Hindustan Times** adds: The four countries signed the "Badr Memorandum of Understanding" in Doha, signalling their intention to deepen defence ties.

**The Hindu** adds: The development comes months after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by Al Jazeera, Dawn Pakistan, The Hindu, Hindustan Times, Anadolu Agency and Times of India Top Stories. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
